ζα.def: ζα insep. Prefix, = δα-, ἀρι-, ἐρι-, very, as in ζά-θεος, ζά-κοτος, ζα-μενής, etc.
ζά (aeolic for διά) ζὰ τὰν σὰν ἰδέαν Theocr.

ζαγκλον.def: ζάγκλον, ου, τό, a reaping-hook or sickle, Lat. falx, Sicilian word for δρέπανον, Thuc. Hence Ζάγκλη, the ancient name for Messana.

ζαθεοσ.def: ζά-θεος, η, ον very divine, sacred, Il., etc.

ζαθερησ.def: ζᾰ-θερής, ές (θέρος) very hot, scorching, Anth.

ζακοροσ.def: ζά-κορος, ὁ, ἡ, (For -κορος cf. νεωκόρος.) a temple-servant, being perh. a form of διάκονος, Plut.

ζακοτοσ.def: ζά-κοτος, ον exceeding wroth, Il., Theocr.

ζαλη.def: ζᾰ́λη, ἡ, (perh. from ζέω) the surging of the sea, surge, spray, Aesch., Soph., etc.; πύρπνοος ζάλη, of the fiery rain from Aetna, Aesch.:—metaph., ζάλαι storms, distresses, Pind.

ζαμενεω.gloss: to put forth all one's might
ζαμενεω.def: ζᾰμενέω, to put forth all one's might, Hes. (from ζᾰμενής)

ζαμενησ.def: ζᾰ-μενής, ές (μένος) poet. adj. very strong, mighty, raging, Hhymn., Pind.

ζαπληθησ.def: ζᾰ-πληθής, ές (πλήθω) very full, ζ. γενειάς a thick beard, Aesch.; ζ. Μούσης στόμα full-sounding, Anth.

ζαπλουτοσ.def: ζά-πλουτος, ον very rich, Hdt., Eur. aeolic for διαπρέπω.

ζατρεφησ.def: ζᾰ-τρεφής, ές (τρέφω) well-fed, fat, goodly, Hom.

ζαφλεγησ.def: ζᾰ-φλεγής, ές (φλέγω) full of fire, of men at their prime, Il.

ζαχρειοσ.def: ζα-χρεῖος, ον (χρεία) wanting much: c. gen., ζαχρ. ὁδοῦ one who wants to know the way, Theocr.

ζαχρηησ.def: ζα-χρηής, ές (χράω) (only in pl.) attacking violently, furious, raging, Hom.

ζαχρυσοσ.def: ζά-χρῡσος, ον rich in gold, Eur.

ζαω.def: ζάω I. to live, Hom., etc.; ἐλέγχιστε ζωόντων vilest of living men, Od.; ζώειν καὶ ὁρᾶν φάος ἠελίοιο Il.; ῥεῖα ζώοντες living at ease, of the gods, id.; ζῶν κατακαυθῆναι to be burnt alive, Hdt.:—also, ζῆν ἀπό τινος to live off or on a thing, Theogn., Hdt., etc.:— τὸ ζῆν ζωή, Aesch., etc.: —in a quasi-trans. sense, ἐκ τῶν ἄλλων ὧν ἔζης (= ἃ ἐν τῶι βίωι ἔπραττες) from the other acts of your life, Dem. II. metaph. to be in full life and strength, to be fresh, be strong, ἄτης θύελλαι ζῶσι Aesch.; ἀεὶ ζῆι ταῦτα [νόμιμα] Soph.; ζῶσα φλόξ living fire, Eur.

ζε.def: ζε inseparable Suffix, denoting motion towards:— properly it represents -σδε, as in Ἀθήναζε, θύραζε for Ἀθήνασδε, θύρασδε:—but sometimes found with sg. Nouns, as Ὀλυμπίαζε, Μουνυχίαζε.

ζεγεριεσ.def: ζεγέριες (without mark of gender, a Libyan word) = βουνοί, a kind of mouse, Hdt.

ζεια.def: ζειά mostly in pl. ζειαί, a kind of grain, spelt, a coarse wheat, used as fodder for horses, Od.; like ὀλύραι in Il.; and Hdt. expressly asserts their identity.

ζειδωροσ.def: ζεί-δωρος, ον (δῶρον) zea-giving, as epith. of the earth, ζείδωρος ἄρουρα fruitful corn-land, Hom.

ζειρα.def: ζειρά, ἡ, a wide upper garment, girded about the loins and falling over the feet, Hdt., Xen. (A foreign word.)

ζευγαριον.def: ζευγᾰ́ριον, ου, τό, Dim. of ζεῦγος, a puny team, Ar.

ζευγηλατεω.gloss: to drive a yoke of oxen
ζευγηλατεω.def: ζευγηλᾰτέω, to drive a yoke of oxen, Xen. (from ζευγηλᾰ́της)

ζευγηλατησ.gloss: the driver of a yoke of oxen, teamster
ζευγηλατησ.def: ζευγ-ηλᾰ́της, ου, (ἐλαύνω) the driver of a yoke of oxen, teamster, Xen.

ζευγιτησ.def: ζευγῑ́της, ου, (ζεῦγος) I. yoked in pairs, of soldiers, in the same rank, Plut. II. ζευγῖται, οἱ the third of Solon.'s four classes of Athenian citizens, so called from their being able to keep a team of oxen, ap. Dem.: cf. πεντακοσιομέδιμνοι.

ζευγλα.def: ζεῦγλα, ης, ἡ, (poet. for ζεύγλη, Anth.)

ζευγλη.def: ζεύγλη, ἡ, I. the strap or loop of the yoke (ζυγόν) through which the beasts' heads were put, so that the ζυγόν had two ζεῦγλαι, Il. Hdt., etc. II. the cross-bar of the double rudder, Eur.

ζευγμα.gloss: that which is used for joining, a band, bond
ζευγμα.def: ζεῦγμα, ατος, τό, (ζεύγνυμι) 1. that which is used for joining, a band, bond, τὸ ζ. τοῦ λιμένος the barrier of ships moored across the harbour, Thuc.:— a bridge of boats, Anth.:— a platform formed by lashing several vessels together, Plut. 2. metaph., ζεύγματ’ ἀνάγκης the bonds of necessity, Eur.

ζευγνυμι.def: ζεύγνυμι (from Root ΖΥΓ, as in ζυγῆναι) I. to yoke, put to, ἵππους Hom., etc.; ζ. ἵππους ὑφ’ ἅρματα, ὑφ’ ἅρμασιν, ὑπ’ ὄχεσφιν, ὑπ’ ἀμάξηισιν Il.;—(so in Mid., ἵππους ζεύγνυσθαι to put to one's horses, Hom.);—also of riding horses, to harness, saddle and bridle, ζεῦξαι Πάγασον Pind.:—of chariots, to put to, get ready, id., Eur. 2. to bind, bind fast, Xen.:—Pass., φάρη ἐζευγμέναι having them fastened, Eur. 3. metaph., πότμωι ζυγείς in the yoke of fate, Pind.; ἀνάγκηι, ὁρκίοις ζυγείς Soph., Eur. II. to join together, σανίδες ἐζευγμέναι well-joined, Il. 2. to join in wedlock, Eur.:—in Mid., of the husband, to wed, id.:—Pass. to be married, Soph., Eur. 3. to join opposite banks by bridges, τὸν Ἑλλήσποντον ζεῦξαι Hdt., etc.:—also, γέφυραν ζεῦξαι to form a bridge, id. 4. to undergird ships with ropes, Thuc.

ζευγοσ.gloss: a yoke of beasts, a pair of mules, oxen
ζευγοσ.def: ζεῦγος, εος, (ζεύγνυμι) I. a yoke of beasts, a pair of mules, oxen or horses, Il., etc. 2. the carriage drawn by a pair, a chariot, car, Hdt., etc. II. a pair or couple of any things, id., Aesch.

ζευγοτροφοσ.def: ζευγο-τρόφος, ον keeping a yoke of beasts, Plut.

ζευκτηριοσ.def: ζευκτήριος, η, ον (ζεύγνυμι) I. fit for joining or yoking, γέφυραν γαῖν δυοῖν ζ. Aesch. II. as Subst., ζευκτήριον, τό, ζυγόν, a yoke, id.

ζευξισ.def: ζεῦξις, εως (ζεύγνυμι) I. a yoking or manner of yoking oxen, Hdt. II. a joining, as by a bridge, id.

ζευσ.def: Ζεύς (the obl. cases formed from Δίς, gen. Διός; dat. Διΐ, Δί [ῑ], acc. Δία) (in Poets also, Ζηνός, Ζηνί, Ζῆνα) (in later doric Ζάν, Ζανός, etc.:—) I. Zeus, Lat. Ju-piter, father of gods and men, son of Kronos and Rhea, hence called Κρονίδης, Κρονίων, husband of Hera: —Hom. makes him rule in the lower air (ἀήρ); hence rain and storms come from him, Ζεὺς ὕει, etc.:—in oaths, οὐ μὰ Ζῆνα Hom., attic; so μὰ Δία, νὴ Δία, attic II. Ζεὺς καταχθόνιος, Pluto, Il.

ζεφυριη.def: Ζεφυρίη (= Ζέφυρος,) sc. πνοή the west wind, Od.

ζεφυροσ.def: Ζέφῠρος, ὁ, Zephyrus, the west wind, Lat. Favonius, Hom., etc.; westerly wind, often represented as stormy, Od.; but also as clearing, ὁπότε νέφεα Z. στυφελίξῃ Il. (From ζόφος night, the region of darkness, as Εὖρος from ἕως, the morn.)

ζεω.def: ζέω I. to boil, seethe, of water, Hom.; λέβης ζεῖ the kettle boils, Il. 2. metaph. to boil or bubble up, of the sea, Hdt.; of passion, like Lat. fervere, Aesch., Soph. 3. c. gen. to boil up or over with a thing, ζεῖν ὕδατος καὶ πηλοῦ Plat.; also c. dat., ζ. φθειρσί Luc. II. Causal, to make to boil, θυμόν Anth.

ζηλοδοτηρ.def: ζηλο-δοτήρ, ῆρος, giver of bliss, Anth.

ζηλομανησ.def: ζηλο-μᾰνής, ές (μαίνομαι) mad with jealousy, Anth.

ζηλοσ.def: ζῆλος, ου, (prob. from ζέω) I. eager rivalry, zealous imitation, emulation, a noble passion, opp. to φθόνος (envy), Plat., etc.:—but also jealousy, Hes. 2. c. gen. pers. zeal for one, Soph., Plut. 3. c. gen. rei, rivalry for a thing, Eur.; ζ. πλούτου Plut., etc. II. pass. the object of emulation or desire, happiness, bliss, honour, glory, Soph., Dem. III. of style, extravagance, Plut.:—also, fierceness, NTest.

ζηλοτυπεω.gloss: to be jealous of, to emulate, rival
ζηλοτυπεω.def: ζηλοτῠπέω, I. to be jealous of, to emulate, rival, c. acc. pers., Plat. II. c. acc. rei, to regard with jealous anger, Aeschin. 2. to pretend to, ἀρετήν id.

ζηλοτυπια.def: ζηλοτῠπία, ἡ, jealousy, rivalry, Aeschin., Plut. (from ζηλότῠπος)

ζηλοω.def: ζηλόω, (ζῆλος) I. c. acc. pers. to rival, vie with, emulate, Lat. aemulari, Soph., Thuc., etc.: —in bad sense, to be jealous of, envy, Hes., Theocr.:— absol, to be jealous, NTest. 2. to esteem or pronounce happy, admire, praise, τινά τινος one for a thing, Soph., Ar.: ironical, ζηλῶ σε happy in your ignorance! Eur. II. c. acc. rei, to desire emulously, strive after, Dem.:—Pass., Plat., etc. 2. Pass. also of persons, to be impelled by zeal, NTest.

ζηλωμα.def: ζήλωμα, ατος, τό, I. that which is emulated: in pl. high fortunes, Eur. II. in pl. also emulous efforts, rivalries, Aeschin., Dem. (from ζηλόω)

ζηλωσισ.def: ζήλωσις, εως (from ζηλόω) emulation, imitation, Thuc.

ζηλωτησ.def: ζηλωτής, οῦ, I. an emulator, zealous admirer or follower, Plat., etc. II. a zealot, used to translate Κανανίτης or Καναναῖος (from the Hebr. qana, to glow, be zealous), NTest.

ζηλωτικοσ.def: ζηλωτικός, ή, όν emulous, Arist. (from ζηλωτός)

ζηλωτοσ.gloss: to be emulated, worthy of imitation
ζηλωτοσ.def: ζηλωτός, ή, όν (ζηλόω) 1. to be emulated, worthy of imitation, Plat., Dem. 2. to be deemed happy, to be envied, Theogn., Aesch., etc. 3. of conditions, enviable, blessed, Eur., Ar.

ζημια.def: ζημία I. loss, damage, Lat. damnum, opp. to κέρδος, Plat., etc.; ζημίαν λαβεῖν to sustain loss, Dem. II. a penalty in money, a fine, mulct, ζημίην ἀποτίνειν Hdt.; ὀφείλειν id.; καταβάλλειν Dem.; ζημία ἐπίκειται στατήρ a fine of a stater is imposed, Thuc. 2. generally a penalty, ζ. ἐπιτιθέναι τινί Hdt.; ζ. πρόσκειταί τινι Xen.; θάνατον ζημίαν ἐπιτίθεσθαι, προτιθέναι, τάττειν to make death the penalty, Thuc., etc. III. φανερὰ ζαμία a mere good-for-nothing, a dead loss, Ar. (deriv. uncertain)

ζημιοω.def: ζημιόω, (from ζημία) I. to cause loss or do damage to any one, τινά Plat., etc.:—Pass., μεγάλα ζημιώσεται will suffer great losses, Thuc. II. to fine, amerce, mulct in a sum of money, c. dat. rei, ζ. τινὰ χιλίῃσι δραχμῇσι Hdt.; χρήμασιν Thuc.:— Pass. to be fined or amerced in a thing, c. dat., Plat.; c. acc., τὴν ψυχὴν ζημιώσεαι wilt lose thy life, Hdt. 2. generally to punish, id., Thuc.

ζημιωδησ.def: ζημι-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) causing loss, ruinous, Xen.

ζημιωμα.def: ζημίωμα, ατος, τό, (ζημιόω) a penalty, fine, Luc.; τῆς ἀταξίας for their disorder, Xen.

ζηνοφρων.def: Ζηνό-φρων, ονος, (Ζήν, φρήν) knowing the mind of Zeus, of Apollo, Anth.

ζητα.def: ζῆτα Ζ, ζ, ζῆτα, τό, indecl., sixth letter of Gk. Alphabet: as numeral ζʹ ἑπτά and ἕβδομος (the obsol. ς̀#, i.e. ϝ, vau, the digamma, being retained to represent ἕξ, ἕκτος), but ͵ζ = 7000. Ζ ζ is composed of ς and δ, so that in aeolic it becomes σδ, as Σδεύς κωμάσδω ψιθυρίσδω for Ζεύς κωμάζω ψιθυρίζω reversely, in attic, σδ becomes ζ, Ἀθήναζε θύραζε for Ἀθήνασδε θύρασδε. But ς often disappears in aeolic, where ζά δια, see ζά, ζα-so in aeolic and doric, as we have Δεύς Δάν for Ζεύς Ζάν, δορκάς ζορκάς:—so also ἀρίζηλος for ἀρίδηλος; ἀλαπαδνός from ἀλαπάζω, παιδνός from παίζω:—doric, in the middle of words, it becomes δδ, as θερίδδω for -ίζω, μάδδα for μᾶζα. Zeta, being a double conson., made a short vowel at the end of the foregoing syllable long by position. But Homer used the vowel short before two prop. names, which could not otherwise come into the Hexam., viz. ἄστῠ Ζελείης, ὑλήεσσᾰ Ζάκυνθος.

ζητεω.def: ζητέω I. to seek, seek for, Il., Aesch., etc.; μὴ ζητῶν without seeking, Xen.; τὸ ζητούμενον ἁλωτόν what is sought for may be found, Soph. 2. to enquire for, Xen.: to ask about a thing, id. 3. to search after, search out, Soph., Thuc. 4. to search or inquire into, investigate, Plat., etc.; ζ. τὰ θεῖα Xen., etc. 5. to require, demand, παρὰ τοῦ στρατηγοῦ λόγον ζητοῦντες Dem. II. to seek after, desire, ἀμήχανα Eur. 2. c. inf. to seek to do, Hdt., Aesch., etc. III. to have to seek, feel the want of, Lat. desidero, Hdt.

ζητημα.def: ζήτημα (From ζητέω) I. that which is sought, οὐ ῥᾴδιον ζ. a thing not easy to find, Eur. II. an inquiry, question, Soph., Plat., etc. 2. a search, μητρός after her, Eur.

ζητησιμοσ.def: ζητήσιμος (ζητέω) to be searched, τὰ ζ. places to be beaten for game, Xen.

ζητησισ.gloss: a seeking, seeking for, search for
ζητησισ.def: ζήτησις, εως (ζητέω) 1. a seeking, seeking for, search for a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Soph., etc. 2. a searching, search, ποιέεσθαι ζήτησιν τῶν νεῶν to search the ships, Hdt. 3. inquiry, investigation, Plat.

ζητητεοσ.def: ζητητέος, η, ον (verb. adj. of ζητέω,) I. to be sought, Soph. II. ζητητέον one must seek, Ar.

ζητητησ.def: ζητητής, οῦ, (ζητέω) I. a seeker, inquirer, Plat. II. in pl. commissioners to inquire into state-offences, Dem.

ζητητικοσ.def: ζητητικός, ή, όν (ζητέω) disposed to search or inquire, searching, inquiring, Plat.

ζητητοσ.def: ζητητός, ή, όν (verb. adj. of ζητέω,) sought for, Soph.

ζιζανιον.def: ζιζάνιον, ου, τό, a weed that grows in wheat, prob. Lat. lolium, darnel, in pl., NTest.

ζοοσ.def: ζοός, ή, όν (poet. for ζωός, Theocr.)

ζοφεροσ.def: ζοφερός, ή, όν (ζόφος) dusky, gloomy, Hes., Luc.:— metaph., ζ. φροντίδες Anth.

ζοφοσ.gloss: the gloom of the world below, nether darkness
ζοφοσ.def: ζόφος, ὁ, I. the gloom of the world below, nether darkness, Hom., Aesch.:—generally, gloom, darkness, Hes., Pind. II. the dark quarter, i. e. the west, opposed to ἠώς, Hom.: cf. Ζέφυρος.

ζοφοω.def: ζοφόω, to darken:—Pass. to be or become dark, Anth.

ζυγαστρον.def: ζῠ́γαστρον, ου, τό, (ζεύγνυμι) a chest or box (of board strongly fastened together), Soph., Xen.

ζυγιοσ.def: ζύγιος (ζῠγόν) of or for the yoke, ζ. ἵππος a draught-horse, wheeler, Ar.:—c. gen., θηρῶν ζυγίους ζεύξασα σατίνας having yoked cars to teams of beasts, Eur.

ζυγοδεσμον.def: ζῠγό-δεσμον, ου, τό, a yoke-band, i. e. a band for fastening the yoke to the pole, Il., Plut.

ζυγομαχεω.def: ζῠγο-μᾰχέω, (μάχομαι) to struggle with one's yoke-fellow, generally, to struggle, Dem.

ζυγον.def: ζυγόν (cf. ζεύγνυμι) anything which joins two bodies; and so, I. the yoke or cross-bar tied by the ζυγόδεσμον to the end of the pole, and having ζεῦγλαι (collars or loops) at each end, by which two horses, mules or oxen drew the plough or carriage, Hom., etc.:—metaph., τὸ δούλιον ζ. the yoke of slavery, Hdt.; δουλείας, ἀνάγκης ζ. Soph., Eur.; ἐπιτιθέναι τινὶ ζυγὰ τοῦ μὴ.., so as to prevent.., Xen. 2. a pair, Eur.; κατὰ ζυγά in pairs, Theocr. II. the cross-bar joining the horns of the φόρμιγξ, along which the strings were fastened, Il. III. in pl. the thwarts joining the opposite sides of a ship or boat, the benches, Lat. transtra, Od., Hdt.; in sg., Soph.:—metaph., τὸ πόλεος ζ. Eur. 2. the middle of the three banks in a trireme; metaph., οἱ ἐπὶ ζυγῷ δορός those on the upper bench, Aesch. IV. the beam of the balance, Dem.: — the balance itself, Plat. V. καρχασίου ζ. the yard-arm at the masthead, Pind. VI. a rank or line of soldiers, opp. to a file, Thuc.

ζυγοστατεω.def: ζῠγοστᾰτέω, to weigh by the balance, Luc.

ζυγοστατησ.gloss: a public officer, who looked to the weights.
ζυγοστατησ.def: ζῠγο-στᾰ́της, ου, (ἵστημι) a public officer, who looked to the weights.

ζυγοφοροσ.def: ζῠγο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) bearing the yoke, Eur.

ζυγοω.def: ζῠγόω, (ζυγόν) to yoke together, ζ. κιθάραν to put the cross-bar to the lyre, Luc.

ζυγωθριζω.def: ζῠγωθρίζω, (ζυγόν IV) to weigh, examine, Ar.

ζυμη.def: ζῡ́μη, ἡ, (ζέω) leaven:—metaph. of corruption, falsehood, NTest.

ζωαγρια.def: ζωάγρια (ζωός, ἀγρεύω) reward for life saved, Od., Hdt.; also, like θρεπτήρια, a reward for nursing and rearing one, Il.: c. gen. rei, ζωάγρια μόχθων, νούσων Anth.

ζωαγριοσ.def: ζω-άγριος, η, ον for saving life, Babr.: v. ζω-άγρια.

ζωγραφεω.gloss: to paint from life, to paint
ζωγραφεω.def: ζωγρᾰφέω, to paint from life, to paint, Plat.

ζωγραφια.def: ζωγρᾰφία, ἡ, (from ζωγράφος) the art of painting, Plat., Xen.

ζωγραφικοσ.def: ζωγρᾰφικός, ή, όν skilled in painting, Plat., Xen. (from ζωγράφος)

ζωγραφοσ.def: ζω-γράφος, ὁ, (ζωός, γράφω) one who paints from life or from nature, a painter, Hdt., Plat., etc.

ζωγρεω.def: ζωγρέω (ζωός, ἀγρεύω) I. to take alive, take captive instead of killing, Il., Hdt., etc.:—Pass., id. II. （ζωή, ἀγείρω) to restore to life, revive, Il.

ζωγρια.def: ζωγρία, ἡ, a taking alive, ζωγρίῃ λαμβάνειν or αἱρέειν ζωγρεῖν, Hdt.

ζωδιον.def: ζῴδιον, ου, τό, I. Dim. of ζῷον II, a small figure, Hdt. II. in pl. the signs of the Zodiac, Arist.

ζωη.def: ζωή (ζάω) 1. a living, i. e. one's means of life, substance, Od.; τὴν ζόην ποιεῖσθαι ἀπό or ἔκ τινος to get one's living by.., Hdt., etc. 2. life, existence, Tyrtae., Trag., etc. 3. a way of life, Hdt.

ζωθαλμιοσ.gloss: giving the bloom and freshness of life
ζωθαλμιοσ.def: ζω-θάλμιος, ον (ζωή, θάλλω) giving the bloom and freshness of life, Pind.

ζωμα.gloss: that which is girded, a girded frock
ζωμα.def: ζῶμα, ατος, τό, (ζώννυμι) I. that which is girded, a girded frock or doublet, Od. 2. in Il. the lower part of the θώρηξ, round which the ζωστήρ passed, Il. 3. the drawers worn by athletes, in Prose διάζωμα, id. II. = ζώνη, a woman's girdle, Soph., Anth.

ζωμευμα.def: ζώμευμα, ατος, τό, soup, ζωμεύματα put by way of joke for ὑποζώματα νεώς, Ar. (from ζωμεύω)

ζωμευω.def: ζωμεύω, (ζωμός) to boil into soup, Ar.

ζωμηρυσισ.def: ζωμ-ήρῠσις, εως (ζωμός, ἀρύω) a soup-ladle, Anth.

ζωμιδιον.def: ζωμίδιον, ου, τό, Dim. of ζωμός, a little sauce, Ar.

ζωμοσ.def: ζωμός, ὁ, Lat. jus, sauce to eat with meat, fish, etc., Ar.; ὁ μέλας ζ. the black broth of Spartans, Plut.

ζωνη.def: ζώνη, ἡ, (ζώννυμι) a belt, girdle: I. properly the lower girdle worn by women above the hips, (the upper-girdle, the στρόφιον, being worn under the breasts), Hom. 2. Phrases, λῦσε δὲ παρθενίην ζώνην unloosed her maiden girdle, of the bridegroom, Od.; Mid. of the bride, Anth.:—of men on a march, ζ. λύεσθαι to slacken one's belt, i. e. rest oneself, Hdt.:— of pregnant women, φέρειν ὑπὸ ζώνης, τρέφειν ἐντὸς ζώνης Aesch., Eur.:— εἰς ζώνην δεδόσθαι to be given for girdle-money (as we should say, pin-money), of Oriental queens who had cities given them, Xen. II. the man's belt (in Hom. commonly ζωστήρ), Il., Xen., etc. 2. the part round which the girdle past, the waist, loin, Il.

ζωννυμι.def: ζώννυμι I. to gird, esp. to gird round the loins for a pugilistic conflict, Od., Hes.; ζ. γαῖαν, of Ocean, Anth. II. Mid. ζώννῦμαι, to gird oneself, gird up one's loins, of wrestlers and pugilists, who in early times wore a linen cloth (ζῶμα, διάζωμα) round their loins. 2. generally, to gird up one's loins, prepare for battle, Il.; also c. acc., ζωννύσκετο μίτρην girded on his belt, id.; χαλκὸν ζ. to gird on one's sword, id.

ζωογονεω.def: ζῳογονέω, (ζωός) I. to produce alive, Luc. II. to preserve alive, NTest. (from ζῳογόνος)

ζωογονοσ.def: ζῳο-γόνος, ον (ζῷον, Γείνω) producing animals, generative, name of Apollo, Anth.

ζωομορφοσ.gloss: in the shape of an animal
ζωομορφοσ.def: ζῳό-μορφος, ον (μόρφη) in the shape of an animal, Plut.

ζωον.def: ζῷον (as if contr. from ζώϊον) I. a living being, animal, Hdt., Ar., etc. II. in painting and sculpture, a figure, image, not necessarily of animals, Hdt.; mostly in pl., ζῷα ἐς τὴν ἐσθῆτα ἐγγράφειν id., Plat., etc.; ζῷα γράφεσθαι, ζωγραφεῖν, with a second acc. of the thing painted, ζῷα γράψασθαι τὴν ζεῦξιν τοῦ Βοσπόρου to have the passage of the Bosporus painted, Hdt.

ζωοποιεω.def: ζῳο-ποιέω, (ζῷον) to produce animals, Arist., Luc.

ζωοσ.def: ζωός alive, living, Homer, Hdt., etc.; ζωὸν ἑλεῖν τινά to take prisoner, Il.; ζωὸν λαβεῖν Xen.

ζωοσοφοσ.def: ζωό-σοφος, ον wise unto life, Anth.

ζωοτοκοσ.def: ζῳο-τόκος, ον (τίκτω) producing its young alive, viviparous, Theocr.

ζωοτυποσ.def: ζῳο-τῠ́πος, ον describing to the life, Anth.

ζωοφοροσ.def: ζῳοφόρος, ον (ζῶον) bearing animals: ὁ ζ. (sc. κύκλος), the zodiac, Anth.

ζωπυρεω.gloss: to kindle into flame, light up
ζωπυρεω.def: ζωπυρέω to kindle into flame, light up: metaph., ζ. τάρβος Aesch.; νείκη Eur.

ζωπυρον.def: ζώ-πῠρον, ου, τό, (πῦρ) a spark, ember, Plat., etc.

ζωροποτεω.def: ζωροποτέω, to drink sheer wine, Anth. (from ζωροπότης)

ζωροποτησ.def: ζωρο-πότης, ου, drinking sheer wine, drunken, Anth.

ζωροσ.def: ζωρός, όν (ζάω) pure, sheer, properly of wine without water, Anth.; absol., ζωρός (sc. οἶνος) id.:—comp. in Hom., ζωρότερον δὲ κέραιε mix the wine more pure, i. e. add less water, Il. As the Greeks mixed their wine with water, the phrase ζωρότερον πίνειν came to mean not only, as in Hdt., to drink purer wine than common, but, generally, to drink hard, be a drunkard, like ἀκρατοποτεῖν, Theophr., Luc.

ζωστηρ.def: ζωστήρ, ῆρος, (ζώννυμι) 1. a girdle, in Il. always a warrior's belt or baldric, which passed round the loins and secured the bottom of the θώραξ:—in Od., the belt with which the swineherd girds up his frock. 2. later, = ζώνη, a woman's girdle. 3. metaph. of the encircling sea, Anth.

ζωστρον.def: ζῶστρον, ου, τό, (ζώννυμι) a belt, girdle, Od.

ζωτικοσ.def: ζωτικός, ή, όν (ζάω) 1. full of life, lively, Lat. vivax, Plat.:—adv., ζωτικῶς ἔχειν to be fond of life, Plut. 2. of works of Art, true to life, τὸ ζωτικὸν φαίνεσθαι πῶς ἐνεργάζῃ τοῖς ἀνδριᾶσιν; how do you produce that look of life in your statues? Xen.

ζωφυτοσ.gloss: giving life to plants, fertilising, generative
ζωφυτοσ.def: ζώ-φῠτος, ον (φύω) giving life to plants, fertilising, generative, Aesch., Plut.
